title: function-calling-parse-investigation-ethan
content:
Objective:
Investigate recurring function/tool-calling parsing errors seen in hosted-api -> structured-output routes. Goal is to list repro steps, capture error snippets, what I tried, hypotheses, short-term mitigations, and next actions (who to loop in).

Background:
- Multiple svc owners reported failures where the assistant returned a tool call but the client-side JSON parse fails or required fields missing. Users see: "Failed to parse tool payload" or "Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0".
- Hits are intermittent (approx 0.3% of calls) and spike after model upgrades (notably after model-profile v2026-02-01).
- Reported primarily by product teams using structured-outputs for ticket parsing and by some customers using function-calling with nested objects.

Repro (local):
1) Minimal prompt used in repro harness (python):
   payload = {
       "model": "redwood-7b-instruct",
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Parse this ticket: subject: \"Service down\" body: \"My site is 500\""}],
       "functions": [
           {"name": "create_ticket", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"title": {"type": "string"}, "priority": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["title"]}}
       ]
   }
   resp = requests.post(api_url, json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"})

2) Observed success majority, but ~1/300 responses have non-JSON wrapper or truncated JSON in the tool call content. Example of failing assistant response body (raw returned from API):
   {"id": "resp-abc123", "choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "<html>503 Service</html>", "function_call": {"name": "create_ticket", "arguments": "{\"title\": \"Service down\", \"priority\": \"high\"}"}}]} }
   - Parser on client attempts json.loads(assistant_msg["function_call"]["arguments"]) and gets JSONDecodeError because arguments is HTML-wrapped or contains leading whitespace/newline/garbage.

Error snippets collected from logs:
- "JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"
- "Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0" (JS clients)
- Truncated output: "{\"title\": \"Service down\", \"priority\": \"hi\""

Hypotheses:
- Model sometimes emits extra content before/after arguments block (e.g., assistant role accidentally includes system/HTML noise). Could be model conditioning shift after profile update.
- Serving runtime may be performing streaming + concatenation; race between final chunk and metadata wrapper could truncate or prepend characters.
- Some middle proxy (edge) injects a health banner or HTML if backend slow -> observed "<html>503" in raw output. That would break JSON decoding.
- The function schema has nested objects; model may produce single-quoted JSON or trailing commas (both JSON invalid).
- Charset/encoding mismatch: occasional 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF (BOM) prepended causing some JS parsers to choke (less likely).

Commands/diagnostics tried:
- Replayed failing request in dev harness multiple times to capture raw bytes; saved raw bytes to file and inspected for non-UTF8 sequences (none).
- Added a pre-parse sanitize step on client: strip leading non-{ characters until first '{' and trim after last '}' (temporary mitigation). Reduced visible errors by ~70% in integration tests but this feels brittle.
- Enabled full-response logging in serving-runtime (trace level) for a single 1-hour window and correlated request IDs with reported incidents. Found ~4 instances where the response body (as stored in logs) begins with a 1-line HTML snippet: "<!--Managed by lb-health-check-->\n{\"id\":...\". This implies an upstream LB/edge health insertion for slow responses.
- Forced response compression off, ensured chunk boundaries consistent; no change.
- Re-ran with a different model (redwood-7b-instruct -> redwood-6b-safe) and saw significantly fewer failures. Points to model output variation being a factor.
- Injected stricter function schema (explicit properties + pattern enforcement) and prompted model with explicit output-only instructions ("Return a single JSON object, nothing else"); reduced but didn't eliminate errors.

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Implement robust client-side sanitizer: attempt to locate first '{' that begins a valid JSON and last matching '}'. Wrap with try/except, report original raw payload to logs for diagnostics. Not ideal but reduces customer-visible failures.
- Add server-side pre-parsing: if assistant message.function_call.arguments doesn't parse, run a filler-sanitizer (strip leading garbage, unescape common escapes, replace single-quotes with double-quotes where safe) and attempt to parse with a safer JSON parser.
- Rate-limit/flag requests hitting the edge where LB inserts content; temporarily route through a different gateway for affected customers.

Longer-term work / hypotheses to validate (owners):
- eng-serving-runtime: investigate streaming concatenation path for any possibility of injecting or misordering fragments when head/tail health snippets are present. (Owner: Ashwin)
- infra/load-balancer: check for any health-check or banner insertion on 503/slow backend paths. Confirm LB config doesn't alter bodies for production paths. (Owner: Maya)
- applied-ml: evaluate if model-profile update introduced prompt tokens that cause the model to echo HTML or newline banners. Rollback test on canary and see if errors drop. (Owner: Ethan / applied-ml)

Data we need to collect (for triage):
- Full raw responses (bytes) for each failure; attach to incident ticket. Capture request_id, trace_id, and route.
- Model version & profile used for each failing event.
- Exact client SDK/parsing code (JS vs Python) to see parser sensitivities.
- Edge/gateway logs for same timeframe to detect any inserted content.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are we certain the LB is adding anything, or is the model itself generating HTML-like noise? Need to correlate by looking at raw upstream response (before LB).
- Should we enforce a stricter server-side schema validation and reject any model output that doesn't validate (fail-fast) and force a model re-run? Risk: increases latency and cost.
- Can we improve the model prompt to never emit surrounding punctuation or commentary? Try a forced JSON mode with sampling temperature 0 and top_p low on canary.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- [Ethan] Collect and attach 10 raw failing responses to JIRA-INC-3421 (due 2026-02-18).
- [Ashwin] Add extra tracing to serving-runtime streaming concatenation path and instrument chunk sequence numbers (due 2026-02-19).
- [Maya] Check LB config and run a small ab test to intentionally slow downstream to see if banner insertion occurs (due 2026-02-20).
- [Applied-ML] Run A/B on canary with previous model-profile to see regression correlation (sync w/ Ethan).

Scratch/log dump (examples):
- Raw fail (trimmed): \n  b'<!--Managed by lb-health-check-->\n  {\"id\":\"resp-zz\",\"choices\":[{\"message\":{\"role\":\"assistant\",\"function_call\":{\"name\":\"create_ticket\",\"arguments\":\"{\\\"title\\\": \\\"Service down\\\", \\\"priority\\\": \\\"high\\\"}\"}}}]}'

- Another: assistant.function_call.arguments = '\n  "{\n    \"title\": \"Service down\",\n    \"priority\": \"high\"\n  }\n\n  '  (note trailing blank lines + extra newline prefix)

Notes/observations:
- Client-side sanitizers mask the symptom; we need root cause.
- Errors correlate with higher p50 latency for the model endpoint; likely interplay between LB heuristics and streaming assembly.
- Model changes reduce but don't eliminate failures, so multiple contributing factors likely.

If you have additional test ideas or want me to scope an infra/serving PR that forces server-side JSON normalization, ping me. I'll keep updating this doc as we collect artifacts.

-- Ethan
